title: A deep, adaptive thinker: loop as long as needed, more layers, more thinking room

brief.state:
B2 (3,302,481 params) runs two weight-shared controller blocks (width 256) for 8 fixed rounds. Each round passes 17 controller vectors (8 control, 9 register) over 27 workspace slots and every reader position. Round t = 1..7 writes program step t, so programs stop at 7 steps (progparse.py N_RES = 7). Rounds 8+ write nothing, and the step embedding stops changing after row 7.

Six confirm seeds (200-205, results/33-pc-confirm-b2): pooled-5 74.02 (73.00-74.74), chain-5 99.4-99.7, +20.3 over plain_tf and +6.9 over plain_tf_steps (both 6 of 6 seeds). Extra rounds at test hurt: in_dist at 16 minus 8 is -0.81 to -1.91 (mean -1.46); screen seeds 100/101 give -1.1 and -0.8. Fewer rounds collapse chain-5 (loops:1 0.0-2.9, loops:2 1.1-6.5). Overthinking (right before round 8, wrong at 8) is 1.7-1.9% of in_dist, under the 2% halting gate. Controller-state size grows about linearly (x3.4-3.9 over 8 rounds), so the blow-up gate stayed shut. The more-loops gate (G1) opened only on its 5%-of-wrong clause: 7.3-8.4% of wrong rows are right at a later round, about 0.8% of in_dist, and no family gains 3 points. Test LR (answer loss at every round) gained +1.1/+1.3 pooled-5, failed stability on seed 200 (-0.51 vs -0.3) and leaked (loops:0 15.88); the arm was stopped, not proved wrong.

Losses sit in families with no program (fewshot_number_rule -14.9 and rule_apply -4.8 against plain_tf_steps over six seeds and five splits), where answers flip across rounds. Controls 2-7 matter strongly on seed 200 only (zeroing costs -7.8 chain-5); seeds 201 and 202 lose 0.6 and 1.0.

Sealed but not run: W1 (global attention in the reader, +33,632 params, queue 42), T1 (calculator as a text tool, 3,277,393 params, queue 40; still at most 7 calls per turn), H1 (learned stop, cap 32; needs the T1 screen first; no stop head coded). W2 (16 scratch tokens) has proposed marks only. Ben's deploy rule requires the model to choose its own round count; B2 still uses fixed rounds (12 under the 8a spec).

open_questions: Does the final-readout blind spot matter? Only programs whose last write falls in the final round are affected (7 steps now, 11 under 8a). A test would add one round after the last write, or write before the blocks, scored on 7-step rows only. Not run.
What fixes no-program families (fewshot_number_rule, list_index, rule_apply), whose answers flip across rounds? Test LR's stability fix failed on seed 200 only and was never run on six seeds.
Why do controls 2-7 matter on seed 200 (-7.8 chain-5) and barely on 201-202 (-0.6, -1.0)? ctl27 has only three seeds; six seeds are needed before any claim that the controls are used scratch.
Can a learned stop avoid truncating programs (rule 7)? Options: per-row K of at least L+1, or stop only after the NOOP that ends a program. Untested.
Is the NOOP (program finished) already the stop for program families, leaving a learned stop useful only for no-program families where no NOOP exists? Untested.
Size of the prize from perfect stopping: the overthinking rows (1.7-1.9%) plus right-later rows (about 0.8%) bound in_dist gains at roughly 2-3 points (suggested, not measured).
Does per-round supervision (Test LR) fix or worsen the zero-round leak? It gave 15.88 on seed 200 and 0.00 on seed 201. Needs six seeds with same-machine baselines.
The leak baseline is noisy across machines (same seed 0.00 vs 1.40, and 10.81 vs 4.34). A determinism check is needed before leak marks are compared across arms.
Does extra scratch (W2) help the no-program families? The controls already do scratch work on seed 200. Untested.
Does an 8-block x 12-round thinker beat a same-size plain transformer, and at what speed? The 8a 10M depth check is reported, not gated; speed is untested.

Calls per turn: T1 gives 7 call slots, but roadmap stage 2d asks for chains up to 16 steps. Either the round count or N_RES must grow, and H1's cap of 32 needs step-embedding rows beyond 8. Undecided.
Does the 16-round stability (Test LR mark 2) hold on the six-seed confirm? Only screen data exists (-0.51 and -0.22).

distinct.title: One traced pass: does B2's own NOOP or confidence give a free stop?
distinct.summary: Run each screen checkpoint once for 16 rounds, keep every round's answer, op, NOOP probability and confidence, then replay stop rules offline. It measures NOOP onset against program length, the cost of freezing at the NOOP round, and the AUROC of the model's own confidence. It says whether a zero-parameter stop exists for program rows (the NOOP B2 already trains) and for the 59% of rows with no program, before any stop is built. Shown ceiling for any stop inside 8 rounds is about 2 in-dist points, so the value is compute saving and the rule-10 path, not accuracy.
distinct.change: New script custom_io/probe_trace.py (copy of probe_loops.py; no edit to ledger.py). Per batch of 128 rows sorted by prompt length, call m.run(batch, loops=16, rounds=True) once under no_grad. Snapshot t is the state after K=t+1 loops, so one run holds all K. Re-apply mode_head, the answer pointer (q_ans, k_slot, valid) and word pointer to ln_z(Z[:,1]) of each snapshot; take op argmax from out['steps'] (rounds 2 to 8 only). Save per-row arrays (probe_loops.py computes them in memory but writes aggregates only): exact_r, answer string per round, mode_p_r, pointer top-1 and entropy, noop_p_r, op_r, and gold program length L (used for grouping only). Arms scored offline: (a) round 8; (b) NOOP stop, t* = first non-NOOP-after-write round, answer read at K=t*+1 and K=t*+2, rows with no t* read at 8; (c) answer-agreement stop for no-program rows (first K>=4 with identical answers at K-2, K-1, K); (d) rows whose step-1 op is NOOP read at pass 6, others at 8; (e) AUROC of conf_r (mode_p times pointer top-1; GEN rows use mean top-1 over the 9 registers), mode_p, ans_top and step-1 NOOP probability for 'already right at r' and 'settled by r' on the 4,007 no-program rows; (f) argmax-confidence over passes 2 to 8 as a selection arm. Extend scoring from in_dist to the five dev splits and chain-5, and add a robust overthinking count (wrong at 8, right at both K and K+1) to price the prize on variant, answer, frame and vocab. Self-check: per-K exact from the trace must equal untraced evaluate at K=8 and 16 on the same machine. Params 0.
distinct.why: Halting alone is capped near 2 in-dist points and about 0.6 pooled-5 points, and 94 to 95% of the overthinking rows and the whole 16-minus-8 loss sit in no-program rows, which carry NOOP targets only at weight 0.1. For program rows the model already trains NOOP after the last write at weight 1.0 but nothing reads it. Freezing program rows at the NOOP round itself costs -3.4 and -5.7 points because the answer heads are only trained at round 8, while one settle round later is nearly free (-0.1 to -0.24 points, 15% of rounds saved). So the open question is whether the model's existing outputs mark the right stop round on each row type; this probe answers it in about an hour on CPU and decides whether ideas 5 and 7 are worth building.

evidence.claim: Overthinking (wrong at 8, right at some round 1-7) is 130 rows (1.91%) and 113 rows (1.66%) of 6,800 in_dist rows; right-later (wrong at 8, right at a round 9-16) is 53 of 724 and 54 of 644 wrong rows. The union is the gold-picked oracle of 2.69 and 2.46 points; it reads untrained heads and counts lucky hits.

evidence.claim: 122 of 130 and 107 of 113 overthinking rows lie in the 19 zero-coverage families. The 16-minus-8 loss is -75 of -78 rows (seed 100) and -58 of -58 (seed 101) in no-program rows (L=0, 4,007 of 6,800 rows).

distinct.summary: progparse drops every program longer than 7 steps to an empty target, so those rows train answer-only, which rule 7 forbids; the documented count is 528 train rows (list_stats, 9 to 11 steps) but it was never recounted. This idea counts the shortfall by family with a reason histogram, then raises the cap at test on hand-built 6 to 9 step rows to see whether the cap or the training coverage binds. distinct.title: Train the model's own NOOP into a per-row stop with freeze
distinct.summary: Make the op head's NOOP after the last write (or a tenth ANSWER class on T1) end each row's loop: the row's state freezes, its answer is read one settle round later, and the answer heads are trained at that round. A cheap screen first fine-tunes the existing B2 checkpoints for 2,000 updates with and without the freeze; a full retrain happens only if that passes. It covers program rows (41% of in_dist) and gives the model a stop it emits itself.
distinct.change: ledger.py run(freeze=False default, which reproduces B2 exactly): per-row done and wrote masks; at the top of each round save Z0; after the blocks Z = where(done, Z0, Z); for 1<=t<=N_RES stop = alive & (op==0) & wrote, writes masked for done rows; readout uses the frozen Z, Rs, vals at round t*+1 (one settle round, an architecture constant). loss() calls run(gold=g, freeze=True) so the gold op drives the stop in training; round_readout stays 0. Eval uses the model's own argmax. Eval-only per-row compaction: gather alive rows, run the blocks on the subset, scatter back (outputs must match the masked full batch exactly; batch-level early exit is useless because 58.9% of rows never stop). Optional arm: w_noop 0.1 to 1.0 (ledger.py:130) if idea 1 finds a false-freeze rate above 2% on L=0 rows. distinct.summary: A probe on the screen checkpoints that labels each wrong variant row in a programmed family by its first wrong link, ranks the gold op at failing steps, counts oracle@k over rank-2 alternatives, tests whether control-token noise gives different still-accurate programs, and counts failed calculator steps a retry could fix.
